Binary Li/Na sulfides retain alkali-S cohesion but lack the P-S charge-partitioning channel.

principle_book.micro_mechanism: Si-N covalency can reduce framework strain relative to Mg-Si-O, but only when Mg-N coordination remains dense enough to maintain ionic cohesion. accepted_mechanisms.claim: Li-Mn oxophosphate stabilization is Mn-specific phosphate separation, bounded by compact Li-Mn oxide stability.
accepted_mechanisms.rationale_summary: Completed rounds support only a narrow Li-Mn-O-P advantage. Fe/V transfer failed, dense/open compactness was ambiguous, and compact Li-Mn-O controls beat compact phosphates in round 3.
accepted_mechanisms.causal_driver: Mn bond-valence and Jahn-Teller strain relief from phosphate-separated oxygen networks.
accepted_mechanisms.intervention: Compare Li-Mn-O-P against P-free Li-Mn-O within matched moderate-density and compact windows.
controlled_variables: Fix Li and Mn; exclude Fe and V substitution.
Match nsites, density, volume per atom, and band gap.
descriptor_predictions: Moderate-density Li-Mn-O-P should lower mean e_hull versus matched Li-Mn-O.
Compact Li-Mn-O controls should match or beat compact Li-Mn-O-P.
failure_modes: P-free Li-Mn-O wins in both moderate and compact windows.
Phosphate advantage appears only in compact Li-Mn-O-P candidates.
evidence_chain: Round 1 supported Li-Mn-O-P over Li-Mn-O but failed for Li-Fe.
Round 3 support_rate was 0.0: compact Li-Mn-O controls slightly beat compact phosphates.
counterevidence_considered: Round 2 support_rate was 0.5, but dense/open splitting did not validate compactness.
No completed evidence directly separates PO4 from pyrophosphate topology.
accepted_mechanisms.scope: Li-Mn-O-P versus Li-Mn-O inside the active oxophosphate program.
expected_material_signs: Primary branch contains Li, Mn, O, and P.
Useful primaries have moderate density or larger volume per atom than compact oxides.
do_not_generalize_to: All dense or compact Li-Mn-O-P phases.
testable_implications: Use executable P-present versus P-absent matched-pair branches.
Treat topology proxies as exploratory, not as the established mechanism.

accepted_predictions.claim: Moderate-density Li-Mn oxophosphates will have lower mean e_hull than matched P-free Li-Mn oxides.

matching_notes: Executable pools: primary 127 matches/32 formulas; control 11 matches/8 formulas.
Compact branch underfills: primary 4 matches/2 formulas; budget reserved for moderate-density test.

falsification_criteria: Primary mean e_hull is not lower than control mean e_hull.
Controls contain equal or more SUN outcomes than primaries.

accepted_bundles.rationale_summary: Accepts F's repair in exploitation mode. The bundle preserves the accepted Li-Mn oxophosphate versus matched P-free Li-Mn oxide test, with comparable Li/Mn/O chemistry, density, nsites, band-gap, and volume-per-atom windows. Candidate-pool checks show adequate availability: primary 140 matches across 36 formulas; control 13 matches across 9 formulas.
accepted_bundles.selection_notes: Use the accepted C/D deterministic order without the added formula tie-break. Material_id is retained only as final duplicate bookkeeping; the intended intervention remains phosphate inclusion versus P-free oxide.

principle_postmortem.current_principle_statement: Moderate-density Li-Mn oxophosphates are stabilized relative to matched P-free Li-Mn oxides when phosphate-separated oxygen networks relieve Mn bond-valence and Jahn-Teller strain; the effect should not be generalized to Fe/V systems or compact Li-Mn oxide-like regimes.
principle_postmortem.micro_mechanism: PO4-separated oxygen sublattices can reduce edge-sharing Mn-O-Mn connectivity, distribute Li/Mn coordination strain, and accommodate Mn-centered Jahn-Teller distortions better than comparable moderate-density P-free Li-Mn oxides. In compact regimes, dense Li-Mn-O frameworks can already satisfy Mn coordination and electrostatic packing, removing or reversing the phosphate advantage.
principle_postmortem.causal_interpretation: Round 5 supports the narrowed mechanism: within matched moderate-density Li-Mn chemistry, oxophosphates have much lower mean e_hull than P-free controls. This is relative stabilization, not discovery, because no SUN outcomes occurred and the control branch contains the lowest single e_hull. The prior compact contradiction remains a real boundary: phosphate separation helps only where the oxide alternative is structurally strained or under-connected, not where compact Li-Mn-O packing is already favorable.
failure_boundaries: No absolute stability or SUN discovery is supported.
Do not transfer to Li-Fe-O-P or Li-V-O-P without oxidation-state-specific evidence.
Do not apply to compact Li-Mn regimes where P-free oxides can match or beat phosphates.
Single low-e_hull control outliers are not explained by the current phosphate mechanism.
unresolved_contradictions: Why Fe phosphate chemistry failed under current matching despite known Fe phosphate cathode stability.
Whether Mn oxidation-state distribution, not phosphate topology alone, is the true causal separator.
Whether PO4 versus P2O7 motifs determine the supported moderate-density window.
Why the lowest individual round-5 e_hull is a P-free control despite lower primary mean.
principle_postmortem.next_test_focus: Within Li-Mn-O-P at moderate density, compare PO4-dominated versus condensed/polyphosphate or mixed-anion topologies under matched Mn oxidation proxy, nsites, density, volume per atom, and band gap; falsify if topology or oxidation-state matching removes the oxophosphate advantage.
